Attendance and Absence
Pupil Attendance
Each day at school represents a valuable opportunity for students to engage learn and grow. Regular attendance not only fosters consistent learning but also instils a sense of responsibility, discipline and a commitment to one's education. We place great emphasis on the significance of attendance and encourage every student to be present and actively participate in their education journey.
What do I do if my child is unwell?
If your child is unwell, please call the school on 01264 352060 or email the school on adminoffice@portway-jun.hants.sch.uk as soon as possible on the first day of and every day of absence until their return to school.
PORTWAY JUNIOR SCHOOL ATTENDANCE 2023-2024 (Whole School)
Full Year Attendance: 96%
Full Year Auth. Absent: 2.7%
Full Year Unauth. Absent: 1.4%
The Law on School Attendance
The law entitles every child of compulsory school age to an efficient, full-time education suitable to their age, aptitude, and any special educational need they may have. It is the legal responsibility of every parent to make sure their child receives that education either attendance at a school or education otherwise than at a school.
When parents decide to have their child registered at school, they have an additional legal duty to ensure their child attends that school regularly. This means their child must attend every day that the school is open, except in a small number of allowable circumstances such as being too ill to attend or being given permission for an absence in advance from the school.
Good attendance at school is important. Statistics show a direct link between high achievement and attendance above 95%. Regular attenders make better progress, both socially and academically, this enables them to find school routines, school work and friendships easier to cope with.
In turn, this means that pupils find learning more satisfying and are more successful in transferring from primary to secondary school. Attendance of more than 95% through primary school and secondary school has a direct impact on pupils' achievement at GCSE standard.
Term Time Absence
Absence during term time is not authorised unless in exceptional circumstances. Term times are for education; this is the priority. If an event can reasonably be scheduled outside of term time, it will not be authorised. Absence during term time for holidays is therefore not considered an exceptional circumstance. Absences to visit family members are also not granted during term time if they could be scheduled for holiday periods or outside of school hours.
If you are unsure whether your child is well enough to be at school, either call the office who will be more than happy to advise or follow the links below for advice:

Information, Medical Forms and Absence Request
Pharmacy First
We'd like to introduce Pharmacy First. This service enables patients to be referred to, or walk into, a community pharmacy for a minor illness or an urgent medicine supply. The link to the Pharmacy First webpage is HERE.
The new service was launched in January 2024 and enables community pharmacies to provide treatment for common medical conditions. There are five conditions that commonly affect children that are included in the service.
Vaccinations
While children can build up some immunity to flu, the virus constantly changes and our body’s immune system cannot keep up with this change, so immunity is only temporary. The best way for children to have maximum protection is by taking up the offer of the free vaccine, which for most children is offered as a painless nasal spray dose.
Healthier Together
We also want to promote the Healthier Together app which is a great source of information for parents and carers across Hampshire and the Isle of Wight. The app, which can be easily downloaded (see Home :: Healthier Together (what0-18.nhs.uk), provides parents and carers with information to help keep their child safe and healthy, as well as helping them decide what to do when their child is unwell.

Parents Information
Welcome, parents, to our dedicated resource page. We understand your involvement is vital in your child's educational journey, and this page is designed to keep you informed. Explore the various sections from attendance to the latest news.
You can see the most frequently asked questions about the school by clicking the below. For any other inquiries or assistance please feel free to contact us. at the school office.
Portway FAQs
Your go-to resource for answers to the most common questions about our school. We understand that choosing the right school for your child is a big decision, and we want to provide you with all you need to make an informed choice.
What are the Office Hours?
The office is manned from 8.30am-4:30pm Monday - Thursday and 8:30am-4:00pm on Fridays, an answerphone is available at other times.
What do I do if I have queries and questions?
Should you have any queries or questions please speak to Mrs Natalie Hammerton or Miss Kelly Miall - Senior Admin Assistants - who will help you or pass you on to the correct person. Teaching and learning queries will be dealt with by your child's class teacher.
What are the school opening times?
Staff welcome pupils at the gates from 8:40am and classroom doors are open from 8:45am when children come straight into class to begin learning at 8.50am. Registers close by 9:00am School finishes at 3.20pm.
What do I do if my child is sick or absent?
Absences must be reported to the office by 10.00am on the first day of absence, and each day thereafter. If your child is unwell with vomiting and or diarrhoea, they must not return to school until 48 hours after the last bout of illness. This follows national health and safety guidelines.
How do I pay for things securely at the school?
ScoPay is our online payment platform used for paying for school meals, milk, trips, and more. It is a cashless system that eliminates the risk of pupils losing or having their money stolen. Parents can credit their child's account online using a debit card through the website. You can login and sign up for an account here: ScoPay Login

Portway Plus+
Portway Junior School have an after-school care facility called Portway Plus.
The club is run by a team of play-workers and a manager. Our manager is well-known to the Portway community, we are thrilled to have Miss Clarke leading the club .
Portway Plus+ is based in the junior school dining hall but also makes use of some of our school facilities too. Activities are very play-based and planned around the interests and ages of the children attending; each session includes a light snack. Sessions run from the end of the school day at 3.20 pm until 5.30 pm and cost £11. We are happy to accept childcare vouchers but we will need notice to register with each different provider.
If you would like to book places for your child/children you will need to fill in a Portway Plus+ User Agreement and Registration Form, Please see below, or you can collect them from the school office. Curriculum
Curriculum Aim:
At Portway Junior School, our vision is to be the pride of our community - where every child is inspired to achieve great things and every family feels welcomed and valued. Through expert teaching and a rich, board curriculum, we aim to ensure every pupil makes excellent progress and is fully prepared for the next stage of their learning and for life beyond school.
We are dedicated to nurturing positive, resilient learners who:
- Are curious, enthusiastic and engaged in their learning
- Show integrity, respect and kindness in all they do
- Support and encourage one another to succeed
- Embrace challenges and are proud of their achievements
We believe in unlocking the potential of every child, building strong foundations for their future and empowering them to become confident, caring and capable citizens in our ever-changing world.
Curriculum Offer:
At Portway Junior School, we offer a curriculum designed to spark curiosity, nurture talents and help every child thrive. We believe that every child is unique and full of potential, and our rich, broad curriculum provides the opportunities, experiences and support needed for them to shine - both now and in the future.
A world of opportunities.
From the very start, Portway children enjoy a wide range of inspiring experiences:
- Engaging lessons in every subject from science and history to art and computing.
- Outdoor adventures through Forest School, building confidence and teamwork.
- Exciting trips, visitors, clubs and special curriculum days to broaden horizons and make learning memorable.
- A special Year 6 graduation with a guest speaker from Winchester University, raising aspirations for the future.
Nurturing the whole child.
Our curriculum is about more than just academic success. We help children to:
- Build confidence, self-worth and pride in their achievements.
- Develop key skills like resilience, empathy, collaboration, critical thinking and creativity.
- Become positive, respectful and independent learners - ready for secondary school and beyond.
Inclusion and high expectations.
We are proud to be a welcoming, inclusive community. Every child regardless of background, ability or needs - is supported to succeed and feel valued. We work closely with families, including those from our military community, to ensure everyone's needs are met.
Building strong foundations for the future.
Our curriculum is carefully structured to:
- Ensure progression in skills and knowledge across all year groups.
- Make purposeful links between subjects for meaningful learning.
- Promote British values and celebrate the diversity of our community.
- Support excellent physical and mental wellbeing.
- Prepare children for a changing, technological world.
We keep parents informed with regular year group newsletters, sharing what your child will be learning each half term. These are also available under the year group page on this website.
We are proud to offer a curriculum that inspires, challenges and celebrates every child - helping them to grow as confident, caring and successful individuals.
To discover more about our curriculum offer or for further information, please contact Mr Anderson via the school office.
Art
We believe that creativity shapes thoughtful, versatile and successful learners. Art, at its core, is the expression or application of human creativity and therefore takes a prominent position in our curriculum. There is great pleasure to be derived from art and design and pupils will learn how it shapes our history and cultures from around the globe.
Computing
The teaching of our Computing curriculum prepares students to use a computer as an aid throughout the rest of their lives, especially as they journey onto secondary school. Pupils understand how to use various software and pieces of technology to support them and their learning. They have a deep understanding of how they can use technology to fit their needs in an ever changing world that relies more and more on technology.
Design Technology
Our Design Technology curriculum aims to inspire pupils to be innovative and creative thinkers who have an appreciation for the product design cycle. We want to provide our children with the opportunities, responsibilities, and experiences they need to be innovative, resourceful and creative problem solvers.
ENGLISH, READING & WRITING
English, Reading & Writing
We are committed to providing a rich and comprehensive English curriculum that equips our students with the necessary skills to become confident, articulate communicators.
Forest School
We embrace the Forest School approach as a unique method of outdoor learning. Our core values of positivity, resilience, integrity, dedication, and encouragement underpin our commitment to inspire and uplift children through enriching outdoor experiences.
Geography
We seek to instil a life-long love of Geography through developing children’s knowledge of the world, as well as their place within it. We aim to deliver a high-quality geography curriculum by teaching our children about diverse places, people, environments and cultures and inspire them to seek new experiences in the wider world.
History
The study of history ignites children’s curiosity about the past in Britain and the wider world and enables them to understand how and why the world, our country, culture and local community have developed over time. We believe that history should provide children with exciting and engaging learning opportunities.
Languages
We aim to provide a relevant, broad and vibrant foreign languages curriculum which inspires and excites our pupils. In line with provision delivered by our link secondary schools, we teach French ensuring that our pupils progress within each academic year and that this range of skills and vocabulary is extended year upon year.
Mathematics
We aim to facilitate an exciting and purposeful curriculum. Children will be taught key skills and strategies so that they are better able to use mental and written methods to solve a wide range of arithmetic, reasoning and problem solving calculations and questions. We believe the teaching and learning of times tables is crucial as it is a fundamental life-long skill.
Music
The music curriculum at Portway Junior School intends to provide a high-quality music education that engages, inspires and challenges pupils. Our objective is to ensure that all children have the opportunity to develop a love for music and to deepen their understanding of music across different cultures, genres and styles.
PE
Portway Junior School recognises the vital role of Physical Education (PE) in fostering physical and emotional development, as well as promoting good health in a safe and supportive environment. Our objective is to provide high-quality PE instruction that not only inspires children to excel in physical activities but also equips them with essential life skills.
PSHE
PSHE reflects our ethos and values. We endeavour to support our children to become independent, confident, responsible and healthy members of society equipped for the ever-changing world in which we live.
RE
We are passionate about preparing children for the next stage of their educational journey as well as preparing them to be moral citizens in the ever changing world they are part of.
Science
The science curriculum will encourage children to wonder at the world around them. Through scientific discussion and inquiry, the children will gain the necessary substantive knowledge and disciplinary skills to build a strong foundation for investigative science as well as motivating their desire to understand ‘why’ the world works as it does.
Safeguarding
Assemblies regularly and throughout the year focused on kindness, empathy, developing good relationships ,anti-bullying ,responsible behaviour, staying safe online .
Personal safety and staying safe when out and about (e.g. road & safety in the dark, summer safety etc.)

Pride of Portway
Learning Together, Achieving Forever, Soaring with PRIDE.
Vision & Values
Our vision for Portway Junior School is to be the pride of our community; to enable great progress for every pupil through expert teaching and a broad and balanced curriculum that prepares our pupils well for their futures. Our aim is for our school community to be positive, resilient learners who behave with integrity, are dedicated to their learning and are encouraging of others. We aim to do this by focusing on behavioural values and learning values
Behavioural Values
Ready - Respectful - Safe
At our school, we uphold a strong foundation of behavioural values to be ready, respectful and safe at all times. This revolves around the 3 values.
These values make up The Portway Code which are the values we strive to model within the school. The Portway code serves as a beacon of guidance for our young students. "Ready, Respectful, Safe" is more than simply a slogan; it represents a way of life that develops our children into accountable, empathetic, and self-assured people.

To be respectful
To be safe

For a deeper understanding of our school vision and values, we invite you to download the vision and values pack. Within its pages, you will learn more about our core principles as a school, and how our values of PRIDE shape our school community.
School Vision and Values
Understanding Our Learning Values
Positivity:
We believe it is important for all pupils and staff to have a positive mindset and attitude to all learning so that we can tackle the challenges that we will face. We understand that mistakes will help us to do this as they are an essential part of our learning. We know that our behavioural values must be lived out in our school all of the time so that we create a positive and calm atmosphere for learning
Resilience:
Staff and children will persist more with their learning in an environment where everyone is respected and with an understanding that life can often be challenging. Together we will show resilience in our learning and in helping each other to achieve personal goals. We will set high expectations of what we can achieve.
Integrity:
Integrity means always doing the right thing, even when no one is looking. Pupils and staff acting with integrity are truthful, dependable, caring, genuine and worthy of trust and respect. They stand up for what is right, show commitment and inner strength and lend a helping hand.
Dedication:
We believe dedication to our learning is vital for everyone to achieve success. Pupils and staff will always give their best, inspiring in each other a passion for learning and serving the school community with integrity and pride.
Encouragement:
We believe that everyone has the opportunity to achieve highly and reach their potential. We believe it is important to create an environment that supports driven individuals and encourages others to join them in the journey to achieve great things. We believe that everyone can contribute to this through the encouragement of each other.
The Portway Code
The Portway Code is a guiding light for our young learners. "Ready, Respectful, Safe" is not just a motto; it is a way of life that helps to shape our students into responsible, compassionate and confident individuals.
